ai.noDataNote: The ML model requires at least 20 rated outcomes to activate. Currently using the physics baseline.
ai.consentGateTitle: Log outcomes to train the AI optimizer
ai.consentGateBody: Enabling outcome logging allows the AI optimizer to learn from your experiment results. Only protocol parameters and outcome ratings are stored, no identifiable sample data.
ai.consentRequired: Enable outcome logging above to use the AI optimizer.
ai.errorNote: Optimizer unavailable. Ensure the Python AI service is running.
ai.guestNote: AI optimization requires an account. Create one to run the optimizer and save your results.
ai.rateOutcomePrompt: How successful was this protocol? (1 = failed, 5 = excellent)
ai.tipOptimizeBtn: AI Protocol Optimizer Uses XGBoost trained on your rated experiment outcomes to suggest optimal protocol parameters. The frontend pre-computes all Schwan physics (τ, fc, selectivity). The Python service adds ML-predicted outcome quality beyond the physics baseline. Requires at least 20 rated outcomes to activate ML. Uses the physics baseline until then.
ai.tipApplyBtn: Apply AI Suggestion Applies the suggested frequency, field intensity, duty cycle, pulse width, and waveform to the sliders. Your current settings will be overwritten.
ai.tipConfidence: Confidence score Blend factor between the physics baseline (0.50) and the ML model (up to 0.90). Grows as more rated outcomes are collected.
ai.tipPhysicsBaseline: Physics Baseline No ML model trained yet (fewer than 20 rated outcomes). This suggestion is derived purely from the Schwan equation: optimal selectivity frequency and lysis-threshold field for the current cell pair.
ai.retrainNoData: Not enough rated outcomes to retrain
ai.lowConfidenceWarning: Confidence is low ({conf}). Rate more outcomes to improve ML accuracy.
ai.tipTrainingSamples: Training sample count The XGBoost model activates after 20 rated outcomes. Each star-rating you submit in the experiment log adds one training sample. The model confidence score grows from 0.50 (physics baseline) towards 0.90 as more samples are collected.
ai.tipRetrainBtn: Retrain Model Triggers the Python XGBoost service to retrain on all rated outcomes in the SQLite database. Do this after collecting a batch of new ratings to refresh the model's recommendations. Requires the Python AI service to be running.
ai.tabExpandTip: AI Protocol Optimizer Click to open the ML-assisted protocol recommendation panel. Rate your experiment outcomes to train the XGBoost model.
ai.calibNoneBody: Log measurements to calibrate the simulator to your bench ({have}/{need})
ai.calibDriftBody: Bench differs from simulator by {pp} pp (n={n})
ai.calibTip: Model Calibration Compares simulator-predicted target and healthy lysis with the measured values you've logged. Shows the mean ∣Δ∣ across all entries with a measured outcome. Tiers: Uncalibrated (n<3), Drift (∣Δ∣>15 pp), Moderate, Strong (n≥10 and ∣Δ∣<5 pp).
ai.calibTipCurrent: Current: {pp} pp off bench (n={n}). Click to open the AI panel for retrain and residual details.
ai.calibTipNone: No bench data yet, calibration idle This chip scores how closely simulator predictions match the measurements you log. So far {have} of {need} measurements are on file, so it has nothing to compare and stays idle. To activate: 1. Run a protocol at the bench and record the measured target and healthy lysis percentages. 2. Open Reports, find the matching log row, and click Log Measured to enter the values. A CSV import with target_lysis_pct and healthy_lysis_pct columns also works. Once enough measurements are logged the chip turns into a live residual badge: Drift (∣Δ∣ over 15 pp), Moderate, or Strong (∣Δ∣ under 5 pp with 10 or more samples). Click the chip to jump straight to Reports.
ai.sigmaCalibNoOrg: Sign in to a lab to calibrate σ_i to your bench measurements.
ai.sigmaCalibTip: Per-cell σ_i calibration Fits a scalar multiplier for each cell's internal conductivity by comparing simulator-predicted disruption ratio with bench-measured lysis. Needs at least 5 measured outcomes per cell preset before a fit is persisted. The multiplier is clamped to the plausibility range [0.3, 3.0]; a clamp warning means the data is pulling the fit outside that range and should be reviewed before trusting the correction.
ai.sigmaCalibResonanceNote: Calibration applies to the Schwan / EP path only; acoustic resonance targets use Q-factor bounds for uncertainty.
ai.applyCalibSubtitle: Base vs corrected predictions at the current protocol
ai.applyCalibHint: Shows how the σ_i multiplier shifts predicted target and healthy disruption ratios, plus the resulting therapeutic index. The live panels already display the corrected values.
ai.applyCalibNote: All values are simulator predictions on the Schwan / EP path. Correction is first-order; compare with measured outcomes in the experiment log for ground truth.
ai.exploreBtnTip: Active-learning suggestion Picks a (frequency, field) point farthest from all your measured log entries in log-space. The goal is to cover under-sampled regions so the next bench run tells you the most about where the simulator and your data disagree. This is a pure exploration heuristic, not a prediction of a good outcome. Use it when you want to widen your coverage rather than refine an already-good window.
ai.retrainModalTitle: Your lab just trained its first model
ai.retrainModalSubtitle: The digital twin is now calibrated to your measured outcomes
ai.retrainModalBody: Future AI optimizer suggestions now blend the shared physics baseline with an ML model fit to the {n} rated outcomes in your log. The model grows stronger each time you rate or log a measured reading; retrain again whenever you collect a batch of new data.
ai.retrainModalTip1: Protocol suggestions reflect patterns in your own bench results, not just population-average physics.
ai.retrainModalTip2: Confidence scores grow past 0.5 as the model learns; treat low-confidence suggestions as exploratory.
ai.retrainModalTip3: Residuals in the Reports view show where the simulator still disagrees with your data. Use them to spot drift.
ai.retrainModalMetricsTitle: Holdout accuracy (20% of your rated entries)
ai.retrainModalMetricsHint: MAE is mean absolute error on held-out entries (0.00 to 1.00 scale), lower is better. A much larger RMSE than MAE means a few outliers are dragging accuracy down.
ai.retrainVerdictInitialTitle: First fit accepted, model {version} is now active
ai.retrainVerdictInitialSub: Holdout MAE: {mae}. All future AI suggestions will blend this fit with the physics baseline.
ai.retrainVerdictPromotedSub: Holdout MAE {mae} beats the previous best of {previous} by {delta}. The new fit has replaced the active model.
ai.retrainVerdictRejectedTitle: New fit did not beat the previous best
ai.retrainVerdictRejectedSub: Holdout MAE {mae} vs previous best {previous}. The active model was kept, log more measured outcomes before retraining again.
